absent: Lock ordering and sleeping constraints for DMA dispatch versus IOMMU and device callbacks.
Exact DMA address width truncation and interaction of coherent mask with streaming masks.
Atomic pool expansion caller contexts and recovery beyond local rollback.
Bounce buffer allocation, synchronization and unmap data paths beyond sizing and area state.
Tracing and DMA API debug event formats and side effects.

findings.text: DMA mapping layer exposes scatter synchronization toward device plus coherent table retrieval, mapping capability test and user area mapping, selecting among a direct path, an IOMMU path, or device supplied callbacks, with a not supported result when no path applies.

Coherent page interface offers allocation and release of page backed DMA ranges plus mapping of those pages into user areas, with public wrappers adding tracing and debug observation around internal dispatch.

Common helpers provide contiguous first page allocation with physical to DMA translation and zeroing, matching release with unmapping, plus single entry table creation and user mapping with protection adjustment and device coherent shortcut.

Noncontiguous coherent interface offers allocation and release of table described ranges together with kernel virtual mapping, unmapping and user mapping, using an IOMMU implementation when present and a single entry fallback otherwise.

Capability queries report whether unmapping or synchronization is required, maximum and preferred mapping sizes, merge boundary and peer to peer support, and allow updating the coherent mask after validation.
Remap helpers expose lookup of pages behind a coherent virtual area and creation of a coherent virtual mapping over a page array with caller supplied protection.
Size arguments for coherent page allocation, release, table creation and user mapping are normalized upward to page granularity before use.

Coherent page allocation fails without dispatch when no coherent mask is programmed and rejects restricted zone, high memory and compound page flags; noncontiguous allocation likewise rejects compound pages and unsupported attributes.
User mappings validate requested page offset range against the number of pages in the allocation and fail with not supported status when the range starts beyond the end or extends past it.
Noncontiguous allocation only permits single page allocation attributes and fallback results are reported as single entry tables with tracing and debug observation on success or failure.

When no boot supplied pool size exists, a default is derived from total memory scaled per gigabyte and clamped between a lower bound and a maximum order limit, then zone specific pools are created only where managed memory exists.

Atomic pool descriptor pairs a confidentiality sharing flag with a generic pool pointer; three zone specific instances exist with separate size counters and a shared target size plus a background work item.

Bounce slot descriptor records original physical location, allocated extent, owning list identity and additional padding slot count; two global booleans control forced bounce and forced disable behavior.
Bounce area descriptor records current usage, area index and a dedicated synchronization primitive.
Physical lookup context carries query address and length together with result virtual address and a found indicator used while scanning generic pool chunks for containment.
Each bounce area is guarded by its own spin synchronization; default bounce memory carries a central lock with a pool list and a deferred work item for dynamic allocation.

Atomic pool memory moves among absent, expanding, ready and failed states; expansion attempts progressively smaller orders, prepares coherence, optionally remaps and decrypts, then publishes to the pool, rolling back mapping and encryption and releasing pages on failure, with background resize triggering expansion when available space falls below target.

Single entry fallback moves among empty, table ready, pages bound and released states; failure at any acquisition step releases earlier resources, and release returns pages before destroying table structures.
Boot time entry points parse a coherent pool size option and initialize atomic pools, background resize work and read only size views.
Scatter synchronization demands a valid transfer direction and treats violation as a fatal programming error; page allocation paths warn once on missing mask or forbidden flags and return null.
Lookup of coherent area pages returns null for absent areas or areas lacking the coherent marker and warns when flags differ from the expected coherent only combination.
Slabs per page constant expresses the ratio between page granularity shift and bounce slab shift.
Minimum bounce slab count corresponds to a one megabyte window expressed in slab units.
Default bounce slab count is initialized from a default byte size converted to slab units, with a separate area count defaulting to zero.
Area count requests normalize zero to one and non power of two values upward, then slab count is enlarged to at least segment size times area count and rounded to a power of two when needed.
Coherent mask updates truncate the supplied value to DMA address width and store it only after a support check succeeds, otherwise reporting an input output error.
Peer to peer support is reported solely from absence of custom mapping operations and deliberately ignores per device bypass state.

Common page allocation prefers contiguous memory before falling back to node allocation, fails cleanly when mapping reports an error by releasing the pages, and otherwise zeroes the allocation before returning.
Common page release unmaps through IOMMU or device callback with CPU synchronization skipped and then releases contiguous backing.

Maximum mapping size returns zero without a DMA mask and otherwise prefers direct then IOMMU then device callback with unlimited fallback; preferred size is the minimum of maximum and an IOMMU or device optimum; merge boundary returns zero when IOMMU absent and no device callback exists.
Zone pool instances are marked read only after initialization to prevent later modification.
Pool size accounting directs added bytes to DMA, DMA32 or kernel counter based on allocation flags.
Contiguous area zone test returns false without area or size and otherwise checks area end against zone limits, with DMA and DMA32 limits applied conditionally and true for generic memory.
Managed DMA32 predicate has build dependent forms selecting either a zone management test or a constant false.
Bounce buffer logging uses a fixed software IO TLB prefix.
Bounce buffer compilation enables trace point creation.
Default bounce memory has alternative declarations for initialized versus plain storage, the initialized form providing lock, pool list and deferred allocation work.
Virtual to page translation distinguishes vmalloc addresses from direct mapped addresses.

Unmap requirement is true for non direct mappings, true when CPU sync skipping is disabled, and otherwise follows whether mapping API debugging is enabled; sync need for direct mappings delegates to a granular address check and is otherwise true.
User mapping without memory management support always fails as not supported; with support it adjusts protection, honors device coherent shortcut, and validates offsets.
Physical to virtual pool lookup scans chunks for full containment of the query range, records translated address on first match, and ignores later chunks once found.
Atomic pool debug views expose three read only unsigned counters for zone sizes under a dedicated directory.
Coherent page array remapping creates a virtual mapping marked coherent and attaches the backing page array to the area for later lookup.
